name: The Tale-Telling Heart
description: A group of people, each with their own story to tell, lights a bonfire at Blue Amber Lake...
chapter: East of the Moon, West of the Sun

dialogs.content: Yes. Since the Proof of the Cognoscenti is well within reach, we might have a chance at getting it too.
It may not be as valuable as the Great Treasure, but it's an essential key for those who covet said treasure...
...Yes. You're right.
I think we could perhaps use it to buy ourselves some time to turn things around... Zhorik, are you listening?
I'm listening. You're right, you're right. However...
So it's a tragedy, isn't it? He gave up the reward, and when he returned home, nothing was the same...
Why tell the story of a fool like him? If it were me, I'd have stayed on that island. Apples aren't my favorite, but that'd hardly be an issue.
Looks like we have new friends joining us.
Hehe, this is a nice place to rest. Are you all telling stories?
Tch, more people...
Zhorik, be nice. Sorry, he's probably feeling unwell. Been like this since we left Novokitezhgrad...
Let us introduce ourselves first. I'm Tolfin. As you can see, I deal in little odds and ends and tell a few stories.
These two are Mr. and Mrs. Shesternin, who are on their way back to Novokitezhgrad from Nasha Town, I believe. This trail is a tough one. Brave of you two to make the attempt.
Ah... We have our reasons for coming here, but that's personal and a long story, so let's leave it at that.
#It's our turn now, right? Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he}{F#she} is {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers, just passing by.
Oh? Then you must have heard of Reed Miller's Great Treasure. They say that the key to unlocking its secret lies within the five <color=#00E1FFFF>Proofs of the Cognoscenti</color>.
Treasure hunting is in the blood of an adventurer.
Speaking of that, I've told many stories about Reed Miller, and I was fortunate enough to lay my eyes on a Proof of the Cognoscenti. One of them was even found by my friend.
Coincidentally, this very spot we're resting at was built by that friend of mine. Knowing him, the Proof of the Cognoscenti might very well be here.
...Are you talking about Papa Wrench?
Oh-ho, it appears my friend is quite famous. Back then, he was traveling between the islands with a caravan, and as it happened, I would have some dealings with them.
Come to think of it, his story is quite extraordinary. Although he lost his memory due to an accident, his skill in crafting and maintaining machinery is as remarkable as ever.
And the very accident that caused his memory loss, that shipwreck from many years ago... I'm sure you've heard of it too, Mr. and Mrs. Shesternin. I believe him to be a survivor of that incident.
That's... Could there be such a coincidence...? Zhorik survived that incident, too... but my father wasn't as lucky.
Danyusha, didn't we agree to leave all that behind?
Yes, I know... but lately I've been thinking... Father loved me — loved us — so much. Were he still alive, he wouldn't sit and let this happen...
Are you two in trouble? Perhaps we could help.
You? Right, you're adventurers... Then, could you find the Great Treasure for us?
Piece of cake.
As long as the treasure exists, we will find it! But, we can't just let you take the Great Treasure off our hands for free either.
Heh, money, money, money... It all comes down to money in the end. Nothing's negotiable without Mora, is that it?
Why are you suddenly so agitated...? You're the one commissioning us to find something for you, so of course you need to compensate us.
We enjoy helping others, sure, but it's not right to expect us to work for free!
Working for free... The Papa Wrench I knew was exactly that sort of person.
Eh? But how would he make a living like that?
He was lucky that the caravan leader looked after him. If it weren't for that, I don't think he would have lasted so long.

He only charged nominal fees for making and repairing machinery. Sometimes he even did it for free. He did the same when it came to teaching others about machines, sharing his knowledge without reserve.
The children in the caravan loved him too, because he had endless stories to tell... Though I should clarify, I could go toe to toe with him on that.
Too bad I didn't prepare candies for my audience like he did, though. His little listeners were, without exception, all captivated by the sweet candies and fantastical stories.
Now you've gotten Paimon all curious about meeting him! It must've been fun listening to his stories... Oh, Paimon wants to hear about how he found the Proof of the Cognoscenti!
Unfortunately, he's no longer with us.
Huh? But you were saying...
He built all the mechanical devices here for a child called Tinet. She was rendered eccentric and hard to get along with by an illness that tormented her.
It took Papa Wrench quite some time to get close to her, too. These devices were originally made to make her happy and fulfill a small wish of hers...
But that poor child didn't make it. After that, Papa Wrench also passed away from his chronic illness and overwhelming grief.
*sigh*... How do you have so many sad stories to tell?

Madam, you're mistaken. Other than tragedies, I also have plenty of stories about righteous bandits robbing the rich to help the poor and tales of underdogs getting their revenge to share. But for now...

Perhaps the two of you could provide some story material. How about a family-friendly treasure-hunting tale? The treasure in this case would, of course, be the Proof of the Cognoscenti that Papa Wrench left behind.
He once said that, should he pass, all his belongings would be mine to handle as I see fit. I'm sure he wouldn't mind a couple of adventurers taking it in exchange for a great story.
"After a thrilling adventure by the mirror-sheened Blue Amber Lake, the two adventurers find the treasure at last." Cliche, perhaps, but a captivating evergreen tale nonetheless.
What do you think?
In that case, we'd be happy to. But umm, rather than our story, could you tell us more about Papa Wrench later?
Haha, no problem. Like I said, all the mechanical devices here were built to make Tinet happy. According to Papa Wrench's vision...

Tinet would need go on a quest like a true adventurer — <color=#00E1FFFF>she'd have to collect lots of Stellafruit, deliver them to Sergeant Octopus, and pass the trial to awaken Colonel Iron Whale</color>.
Then, the "Proof of the Cognoscenti" would be her reward. Hmm, that's all the hints I can give for now. If you two run into any difficulty, just think of this as extra spice in our story.
It's alright, Papa Wrench wouldn't make anything too tough on purpose, right? This should be way easier than those mechanisms in the ruins.
Alright, then! Show me what you're capable of. Sergeant Octopus has command over two areas, and you can start the challenge from either one.
As for you, Mr. and Mrs. Shesternin, since you're just passing through and don't intend to be held up by this treasure hunt, please excuse me if I accompany you no further.
...Of course, but we'll stay here for a little while longer.
Sure, with fair compensation for honest work...
For Paimon's sake, I must obtain the Great Treasure...
#Y—You're doing this for Paimon? Paimon's touched... When we get the Great Treasure, she'll share half of it with you for sure, {NICKNAME}!
Stellafruit only grow near Blue Amber Lake, and the climate here is indeed very different from everywhere else. The atmosphere in the air... is beyond words.
You need to deliver enough Stellafruit before Sergeant Octopus will reveal the trial's contents. Well, since this is a fairy tale, I suppose it doesn't really count as "bribery."
It must be here...
What are you doing here?
Not much. I just wanted to watch your treasure hunt from the place with the best view.
Will I make it in time...?
Are you leaving?
...Oh! Yes, yes. I left something important in Nasha Town, so I should go back...
It seems the device for awakening Colonel Iron Whale is missing some parts. That figures. Even guarded treasures are coveted by others, let alone unguarded ones.
So the Proof of the Cognoscenti... the treasure is hidden here?
It's certainly nearby, but...
Why don't we just take it apart, then? It's little more than a pile of scrap anyway. This way, you won't have to play this little game of pretend anymore. Why not just make things easier?
That's certainly one way to go about it...
Hey! That's... Um, Paimon doesn't think that's right. Papa Wrench poured his heart into this after all. If we can just find the missing parts...
If we're talking about spare parts, I might have some leads.
Wow, are you really giving us clues just like that?
It's not unusual to receive aid from mysterious characters in stories, right? Mr. Shesternin, if you're also interested in the treasure's whereabouts, it's not too late to join us...
Hah! I... I'm a collector, so of course I'm interested in the Proof of the Cognoscenti, but I won't play along with your childish games.
Well, you can certainly try to challenge Colonel Iron Whale your way. Let's see who can locate the treasure first. As for you, adventurers, please follow me.
Time to spice up this story.
Paimon's going to sneeze from all that spice! Hmm... there must be some other way! We just need to find the missing parts, right? Well, we're good at finding things.
Papa Wrench's workshop is down this way. You should be able to find the spare parts there.
Then all we need to do is activate the lift, right? Paimon's got this... Huh? Where's the lever?
Ah! A weasel thief!? Did it steal the lever?
Well, this is... unexpected. Don't worry, I'll handle things from here.
You? But...
Huginn! It's your turn to shine.
Eh!? And where did you come from!?
It's not that unusual for traveling merchants to have a few clever companions, no? Quickly, let's catch up to it.
Just a hunk of metal junk...
Huh? What's going on here?

Hmm, it seems Sergeant Octopus isn't feeling well. Perhaps it's getting aggressive because it's not used to the environment. After all, underground caves aren't exactly where octopuses usually hang out.
Sergeant! Pull yourself together!
Your power is essential in awakening Colonel Iron Whale, Sergeant!... Um, so how exactly do we make it stop?
#Looks like we'll have to get closer to make it stop. Well then, I'll leave it to you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.
I feel like you're implying something here...
I've always respected the audience's freedom of interpretation. However, rather than that which lies between the lines, we have more pressing matters to address right now.
Should I recite a few silly limericks to set the mood? Hmm, perhaps not.
Phew, it finally stopped. Maybe this guy needs a demotion to "Corporal Octopus"!
#It's safe now, {NICKNAME}. Let's look around for the spare parts.
Three humans and a weasel search up and down, until you finally find the spare parts...
Awesome! Now we can go and wake Colonel Iron Whale up, right?
Wh—What's going on? Ah! The path we came from has been blocked!
Oh? It looks like this is becoming quite the spicy story.
The spicier the better!
Whether it's food or adventure, too much spice is bad news!
Don't worry, leave it to Huginn. Treasure-hunting isn't all it can do — it's also good at pathfinding.
You see? Just follow its lead, and we're bound to find something good.
Oh, you... You're not gonna do anything yourself, are you? It's been on us or your Weasel Thief this whole time.
Haha, I suppose it's a kind of family tradition. Those who are bolder oft shall lead the charge, while all we can do is chronicle their feats and sing their praises.
Alright, our adventure isn't over yet. The Proof of the Cognoscenti awaits, so let's head out now.
I can't handle spicy food...
So, you found the spare parts?
Seems you're helpless against this hunk of metal junk.
Hehe, we won! The Proof of the Cognoscenti is ours now!
W—Well... congratulations. But are you really going to activate the device right now? This thing looks like it's been out of use for a while, there might be some malfunction...
Mr. Shesternin, are you worried that such a malfunction might hurt one of us? How thoughtful. However, with the treasure within our reach, it would be too much to ask us to simply ignore it.
#Yeah, that's right! {NICKNAME}, let's install the parts and start it up right now!
Guess it's up to us to awaken Colonel Iron Whale, then!
It's a shame that Tinet couldn't see all this with her own eyes. She would have loved it.
Maybe there are others...
Those shiny things we collected earlier... they look like pictures. But where's the Proof of the Cognoscenti? Paimon doesn't see anything like that at all...
Maybe someone already swiped it...
If someone already took it, then that guy was leading us around all this time, wasn't he? Ugh. That's it. That's one score we've gotta settle!
Hmm... Not that we can do anything about that right now, though. Let's go back first!
The experiences and memories we gain are the most precious of treasures!
Uh huh, and adventurers would've all starved to death long ago if that was always the case!
Haha, you're too late. You didn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti up there, did you?
Huh? How did you...
Sure, but we found something more precious still!
More precious? Impossible...
(Judging by that smug look he's wearing, he probably found the Proof ahead of us. Might as well try to trick him here...)
(Oh? You want me to play along with your little act, then?)
Well... there are five Proofs of the Cognoscenti after all, nor would locating the Great Treasure be a simple affair even after one collects them all.
So... I would hardly be surprised if something in Papa Wrench's collection could far surpass a single Proof in value.
...Such an item exists?
O—Of course! You could call it priceless, even!
#(Paimon has no idea what {NICKNAME}'s up to, but... That isn't exactly a lie, right? Memories are priceless! Besides...)
...J—Just ask Tolfin or something. He'd pick what we've got over the Proof for sure!

And what would a wandering merchant like him know? ... Aha! I get it now, brat. You're bitter because you lost, aren't you? You're upset that I didn't need to play your little game to get the treasure.
I happen to be in a good mood, so I'll pass this advice to you for free: Forget about the rules. People who stick to them hardly ever get the life they desire.
Fortune favors those who think outside the box, like me. See? You did all that work, in the end, you still couldn't find the Proof of the Cognoscenti.
Zhorik takes out a pristine and opulent goblet. It is hard to believe that it also belonged to Papa Wrench's collection...

Ah, yes. It is indeed true that one of the five Proofs of the Cognoscenti is a goblet. But as far as I know, that one is in the Fatui's possession. Many treasure hunters have their eyes on it, in fact.
The Proof that Papa Wrench found was a mask, and he would often let the children play with it.
As for this goblet... I do believe it's a gift the caravan leader brought from Snezhnograd. Ah, but Papa Wrench never could bring himself to use such a precious thing.
#It's valuable, of course, but nothing compared to the Proof of the Cognoscenti... Which in turn makes it even less valuable than the treasure {NICKNAME} found, I fear.
That's impossible...
It appears even a seasoned collector such as you can be mistaken at times, Mr. Shesternin. If it sets your mind at ease, you are free to find an appraiser for it when you return to Novokitezhgrad.
...Where is the real Proof of the Cognoscenti then? No... forget that. What's the treasure you spoke of, kid? The one you claim is the superior find...
You may have beaten me, but I shan't accept it until you've shown me what you found.
Huh? Th—That's...
(The picture and memories might be priceless to Tolfin, but could we really say something like "This is the most valuable treasure!" without embarrassing ourselves!?)
#(Hurry, {NICKNAME}! Think of something!)
(Since there's more to what happened aboard the "Fortunate One" ten years ago...)
Before we show you, take a look at this.
You show the picture from earlier to Zhorik...
...What is this trickery!? Who commissioned you to do this? Was it that old man? Is he still alive? Where is he!?
So you *are* the Zhorik that Papa Wrench mentioned!
"Papa Wrench"... So, he lured me here with a fake name so he can have his revenge, is that it? You think you can take me?
Revenge? What are you talking about?... Wait, so the one who pushed Papa Wrench off the ship was...
Drop the act. You're all working for that old man, aren't you? Wait... Does Danyusha know? Is she in on this too?
That woman... She agreed so quickly because she knew this was a trap all along, didn't she? Offering to deliver the letter, doing all that, just to isolate me...?
That's right. It's over.
No. Not one of you will ever get me! Not you, and not that old man!
Zhorik scurries away, not even bothering with the precious goblet he mistook for the Proof of the Cognoscenti...
Are you just letting him go? We don't have any grudge against him, but isn't Papa Wrench your friend?
Don't worry. The path he took looks most dangerous. I would not be surprised if something happens to him.
What do you mean...?
I mean that Papa Wrench has many other friends aside from me. Besides, who doesn't love a story where justice is served?
I'm afraid ten years wasn't long enough to change his ways. If he had proven himself a changed man, even just a little, then I would have forgiven him, per Papa Wrench's wishes.
Alas, like many others, he too is a prisoner to his baser instincts. What a tragedy.
...What saddens me more is the lack of a winner in our little treasure-hunting game. *sigh* No new story material for me, then.
Oh! Paimon almost forgot — where exactly is the Proof of the Cognoscenti? Will we find it here? Um... can we ask Huginn for help?
Might this be what you're looking for?
A mask... Is this it!? But how... You had it on you this whole time?
Haha, not quite. Zhorik did find it first, but he thought the flashier, fancier goblet was the real Proof, so he tossed the mask aside.
And now that he's forfeited it, the treasure is yours.
Feels like a freebie... but wait! We worked hard for it too! It's our just reward!
That's right. If you end up revealing the Great Treasure's secrets... Well, that would make for a fascinating story.
You're getting ahead of yourself...

I'll go up and take a look.
You can climb up that thing?
#Can we even call ourselves adventurers if we can't even manage that? Hmm, even if {NICKNAME} can't do it, Paimon sure can!
What reliable companions you are. Well then, I hope to hear good news from you soon!
I guess I'll come visit Colonel Iron Whale from time to time.
About the Proofs of the Cognoscenti...
They make for great stories, so I do know a thing or two. Allegedly, there are five Proofs of the Cognoscenti in total.
Besides the one Papa Wrench had, there are two more on the three southern islands. The remaining two are further north. You might find more clues about them in Piramida.
If you're also interested in the Great Treasure, you might want to keep an eye out for them.
About Huginn...
A journey needs empathetic companions, no? It had quite the natural gift, so training it didn't take long at all.
Maybe it's because I have a special connection with weasel thieves — which I suppose you could call a family tradition too, hmm?
Goodbye.
I wish you a lovely journey.
(test)Readable Placeholder
This isn't a spare part... Did Papa Wrench leave this here? So it's like Tolfin said. He stayed for Tinet's sake...
I didn't expect Huginn to dig up something like this. But judging by your words... Did you doubt what I said?
Well, they did come from someone who'd give away a friend's treasure...
#...Huh. When you put it like that, {NICKNAME}, it does sound suspicious! P—Paimon was just playing along earlier, just so you know! We had to see what tricks you had up your sleeve!
#What are you planning now, bringing us to this place?... Best be warned, {NICKNAME}'s super strong!
Haha. To me, you are both unexpected guests, but great "spices" for the story all the same. I can hardly thank you enough. Why would I ever mean you harm?
Well then, let's keep searching for the spare parts. I really don't know where Papa Wrench left the Proof of the Cognoscenti, so it's all on you now.

Same handwriting as earlier... Wait, Danyusha... Zhorik?
Is Danyusha Papa Wrench's daughter, then? But Paimon thought he fell into the sea because of an accident that happened ten years ago aboard the Fortunate One.
*sigh* Huginn, you just had to dig this page out, didn't you? I guess I have no choice but to...
#Paimon knew you were up to no good! {NICKNAME}, draw your sword, quick!
...No choice but to tell you all my plans now, and ask that you pretend you know nothing from this point on.
...Huh?

I was there the day Papa Wrench saw the obituary. He had a strange look on his face, so I asked him about the matter. Even so, he kept insisting that he couldn't remember the details from ten years ago.
Always assuming the best of others... That's just the way he was. Besides, he had Tinet to care for, so everything else took a backseat.
After he passed, I kept my ear to the ground, and what do you know? News reached me that the Shesternins had exhausted their wealth over the last ten years and had landed in serious debt.
So, I sent a messenger to tell a story. "Have you heard? The Proof of the Cognoscenti that can lead you to the Great Treasure is at the Blue Amber Lake in Nod-Krai"...
You were going to give him the Proof of the Cognoscenti?
Technically, it is Papa Wrench... Mr. Shesternin Sr.'s inheritance. As his legal heir, Zhorik has the right to it.
I'm not as charitable as ol' Papa, but I wanted to give Zhorik a chance to prove himself. And that's how the treasure hunt came to be.
He's not interested in the story or the setting, but he seems determined to get the Proof all the same. It's entirely possible that he might find it before you two.
That won't do!
Indeed. Therefore, my plan is to ask you to interfere with the process... or should I say, "finders keepers" — as long as you get it before him, of course.
Though if your conscience permits, you can let him find it first before taking it off his hands. Not a terrible strategy either, that.
So that's your plan... Paimon doesn't get it! Do you want him to have it or not? And, what if we didn't come this way? What was your original plan?
A scheme abandoned hardly matters in the present, does it? I have great faith in your treasure-hunting skills.
When we go back out, please pretend you've heard nothing. It would not do for me to appear biased, after all.
